messages.content: We need to settle the Boston dates before looking at hotels. The family celebration is Saturday January 23. Compare leaving Chicago Thursday evening versus Friday morning, then coming home Monday evening or Tuesday morning. Three travelers, and don't book anything.
I’ll compare all four combinations. Are Marcus, Daniel, and Owen traveling from ORD, and should I count missed school and work time as well as airfare and hotel nights?
Yes, ORD for all three. Owen can miss Friday if needed, but I would rather not also lose Tuesday. Daniel and I can take Friday off. Tuesday would create another work absence for both of us.

The strongest nonstop options are:

Outbound Thursday Jan 21: American, 6:20-9:42 p.m., $267 each. You keep Thursday available and get all day Friday in Boston.
Outbound Friday Jan 22: United, 7:10-10:31 a.m., $219 each. It saves $144 total but gives up Thursday night and most of Friday morning.

Return Monday Jan 25: JetBlue, 6:05-7:58 p.m., $244 each. You retain most of Monday and avoid a Tuesday absence.
Return Tuesday Jan 26: American, 8:20-10:15 a.m., $186 each. It saves $174 total but adds Monday night and costs Owen another school day plus a workday for each adult.
Put those into complete combinations. Use $260 per hotel night including tax so the lodging difference is visible.

Thursday-Monday: airfare $1,533, four hotel nights $1,040, combined $2,573. About three and a half usable days in Boston; Owen misses Friday only, and both adults use Friday only.

Thursday-Tuesday: airfare $1,359, five nights $1,300, combined $2,659. Most Boston time, but Tuesday is lost to travel and the extra night outweighs the airfare savings.

Friday-Monday: airfare $1,389, three nights $780, combined $2,169. Lowest combined cost, but only about two and a half usable days and it is not a four-night trip.

Friday-Tuesday: airfare $1,215, four nights $1,040, combined $2,255. Cheapest four-night pattern, though Owen misses Friday and Tuesday and both adults lose those workdays.
How much actual time do we gain by going Thursday evening instead of Friday morning? Assume we can be out of the airport 45 minutes after landing.

Thursday puts you out of BOS around 10:27 p.m., so that night is mainly arrival and check-in. The real gain is Friday morning: compared with clearing the airport around 11:16 a.m. Friday, you gain roughly four to five usable hours after allowing for breakfast and getting into the city. It also makes Friday less vulnerable to a morning delay.
And Monday evening versus Tuesday morning? I don't want to count sleeping at the hotel as vacation time.

Tuesday morning adds only Monday evening and an unhurried dinner, roughly four usable hours. Tuesday itself contributes no Boston time because you would leave for the airport around 6:15 a.m. That extra time costs one hotel night and three additional weekday absences.
So Thursday through Monday is $404 more than Friday through Monday, but it buys the Friday morning time. Correct?
Correct. The difference is $144 in airfare plus $260 for Thursday night, totaling $404. In return, you arrive settled for Friday and gain about four to five useful hours.
Compare just the two four-night patterns now. I don't think the three-night version is worth pursuing.

Thursday evening-Monday evening is $2,573 and protects Tuesday school and work. Friday morning-Tuesday morning is $2,255, saving $318, but it adds three Tuesday absences and provides only about the same usable time: the later return mostly replaces the Friday morning lost on arrival. Thursday-Monday is therefore the cleaner schedule despite the higher price.

Use Thursday January 21 through Monday January 25 as the dates. Keep Friday January 22 through Tuesday January 26 as the lower-cost fallback for the hotel search, since hotel rates could change the math. No flights yet.

Dates selected, with no booking: primary is Thursday Jan 21 to Monday Jan 25, using American ORD-BOS 6:20-9:42 p.m. and JetBlue BOS-ORD 6:05-7:58 p.m. Airfare for three is $1,533; four estimated hotel nights bring the planning total to $2,573. Owen misses Friday, and Daniel and Marcus each use Friday off.

The lodging-search fallback is Friday Jan 22 to Tuesday Jan 26, using United 7:10-10:31 a.m. outbound and American 8:20-10:15 a.m. return. Airfare is $1,215; with four estimated nights, the planning total is $2,255. It saves $318 but adds Tuesday school and work absences. The Saturday Jan 23 celebration remains fixed.
